title: How Many Meeting Rooms?

concept.title: Sort by start time and keep the end times of the rooms in use in a min-heap
body: Meetings are intervals `[start, end)`. Two meetings can share a room if one ends before (or exactly when) the other starts. The smallest number of rooms equals the **largest number of meetings that are running at the same time**.

Process the meetings in order of **start time**. Keep the **end times of the meetings that occupy rooms** in a min-heap. For a new meeting look at the room that becomes free the earliest (the top of the heap): if it is free already (`end <= start`), the new meeting takes that room, so remove that end time; either way, push the end time of the new meeting. The size of the heap at the end is the number of rooms that were needed.

body.code:
meetings.sort()                          # by start time
heap = []                                # end times of the rooms in use
for start, end in meetings:
    if heap and heap[0] <= start:
        heappop(heap)                    # that room is free: reuse it
    heappush(heap, end)
print(len(heap))

body: A meeting that ends at time 5 does not collide with one that starts at time 5, which is why the test is `<=`. Sorting costs O(n log n) and each meeting does O(log n) heap work.

statement: There are `n` meetings, the `i`-th one lasts from `start` to `end`. A meeting that ends at the moment when another one starts does not collide with it. Print the smallest number of rooms with which all the meetings can be held.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the number of meetings.
Each of the next `n` lines has two numbers `start` and `end` of a meeting.

examples.note: The meeting 0-30 is running during both others; 5-10 and 15-20 can share the second room: 2 rooms.

hints: Sort the meetings by start time.
Keep the end times of the rooms in a min-heap; the top is the room that becomes free first.
If the top is at most the new start, reuse that room (remove the old end time). Push the new end time.

explanation: Meetings are taken in order of start time; a min-heap holds the end times of the rooms in use. A room that is free by the new start is reused, then the new end time is pushed. The heap size is the number of rooms.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
iv = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

import heapq
iv.sort()
heap = []
for start, end in iv:
    if heap and heap[0] <= start:
        heapq.heappop(heap)
    heapq.heappush(heap, end)
print(len(heap))
